extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO final order implementing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: describes procedural steps, statutory/regulatory authority, the factual bases for discipline, and the sanctions/notice obligations imposed on a registered patent attorney based on a state-bar reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a State when a registered practitioner has been disciplined by a State authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the December 16, 2021 Order of the State Bar of Nevada, Northern Nevada Disciplinary Board, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). If the practitioner does not file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose the identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (predicate conduct: state public reprimand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is publicly reprimanded for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being publicly reprimanded by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO discipline here is grounded on the State Bar's public reprimand; the USPTO action mirrors the state disciplinary determination as authorized by statute and regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional-conduct grounds found by State Bar (Rule 1.3 Diligence; Rule 1.15 Safekeeping Property)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Bar of Nevada reprimanded Respondent for violating Rule of Professional Conduct 1.3 (Diligence) and Rule of Professional Conduct 1.15 (Safekeeping Property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific factual findings supporting those violations: while representing two separate clients, Respondent failed to timely prepare patent applications (diligence); Respondent accepted advance payment of fees and did not deposit the fees into a Client Trust Account, so funds were not available for immediate return upon termination of representation (safekeeping). The Disciplinary Board also noted that Respondent had cooperated in the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial sanctions and conditions imposed by disciplinary authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Bar ordered that Respondent open a Client Trust Account (IOLTA), complete four additional Continuing Legal Education credits within 90 days of the Order, and pay Nevada Supreme Court Rule 120 Costs of $1,500 plus the hard costs of the disciplinary proceedings to the State Bar within 30 days of the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These remedial measures were part of the State Bar's discipline and are referenced by the USPTO order; the USPTO imposed a public reprimand and directed publication/notification consistent with its regulatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification obligations under USPTO disciplinary rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish the Notice in the Official Gazette and to give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are made available for public review (e.g., OED FOIA Reading Room URL provided). Publication and cross-notification are routine consequences of USPTO disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural service and timelines for Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. 70220410000250013724 and 70220410000250013731) and was received on November 5, 2022. Respondent had forty (40) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service by certified mail and observance of the 40-day response period are procedural prerequisites; failure to respond within that period supports a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and justification for imposing reciprocal discipline.
